thread:
aj: Heads-up — product team needs a new GPU node pool in canada-central for low-latency embed infer. Expected baseline: 60 concurrent pods, mostly small-batch (<64 tokens) streams. Asking for advice on instance type mix (L4 vs A10G), spot ratio, and autoscaler settings.

maria: How bursty is it? steady baseline or big short spikes?

aj: baseline ~30 pods steady, spikes to 200 for 2–10 min windows during peak tests. want predictable p50 latency under 120ms. budget target ~30% cheaper than our current us-based pools.

kai: for that profile I'd do a mixed pool: majority preemptible L4s for cost, a small guaranteed A10G reserved pool for tail latency + heavy batches. L4 is cheaper per-GPU for small tokens.

sabrina: +1. Also add a tainted small-reserved pool (node taint: gpu=reserved:NoSchedule) for SLA workloads, and set tolerations on those critical deployments.

leo: Autoscaler config thoughts: keep min nodes low (1-2) for reserved pool and min 6 for spot L4 pool. Scale-up fast (cpu-utilization threshold 30 for CA), scale-down delay longer (10m) to avoid churn. Also set max nodes to handle the 200 pod spike: estimate ~40 L4 nodes?

aj: can you share the calc? curious about pod-per-gpu assumptions.

leo: assume 4 pods per L4(1 GPU, 4-way partitioning with MIG-like sharing) for small streams. So 200 pods / 4 = 50 nodes, but with reserved A10G covering heavy ones we can drop ~10 nodes. so max ~40–45 nodes.

kai: If using GKE autoprovisioning, prefer separate node pools with nodeAffinity-based routing. For cluster-autoscaler on GKE, pass flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --max-empty-bulk-delete=10, --balance-similar-node-groups=true. Also enable autoscaler profiles for fast scale-up.

aj: can we use spot preemptible for L4? worried about eviction impact on streams.

sabrina: yes but use pod disruption budgets and a fallback routing policy in the API layer to route long-lived sessions to reserved A10G pool. short inference pods can be retried.

maria: what about quotas and image egress? canada-central has lower GPU quotas historically, we should open a request. infra-bot, can you run a quick quota check?

infra-bot: quota-check: canada-central GPU quota: currently 24 total GPUs, A10G quota: 8, L4 quota: 16. Regional vCPU quota 200. Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/quotas?project=redwood-project&filter=canada-central1

aj: ok quota is too small. I'll file the quota increase and mark this ticket high priority.

kai: alternative if quota increases take time: hybrid strategy across canada-central + us-east1 with smart routing (latency fallback) and cross-region caching. but that's more network egress and cost.

leo: networking: ensure we have VPC peering/private service connect to avoid public egress between regions. also check egress quotas for embeddings traffic — can get expensive.

sabrina: cost tradeoff numbers (back-of-envelope): L4 preemptible $0.05/token-min? (mock), A10G reserved ~3x cost but 2.5x throughput for large batches. we'll run a probe job to get real token-level numbers.

aj: next steps I propose: 1) aj files quota increase request for canada-central GPUs (A10G + L4) 2) create terraform PR defining two node pools: a) l4-spot-pool (taint gpu=spot:NoSchedule, taintKey for eviction), min=6 max=45, tainted pods tolerate, autoscaler CA flags per kai b) reserved-a10g-pool, min=1 max=6, taint gpu=reserved:NoSchedule 3) add kube-probe routing fallback and PDBs 4) run 24h cost/latency probe.

maria: +1. add an annotation to nodepool for billing center and dedicated service account for driver install.

kai: I'll prep the terraform snippet and helm values for nvidia-driver daemonset. Example gcloud create (for quick test):
```\
gcloud compute instance-templates create l4-template \\
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-l4 --preemptible \\
  --image-project=cos-cloud --image-family=cos-stable
```

leo: For cluster-autoscaler we should also set scale-down-utilization-threshold to 0.5 for GPU pools to avoid evicting nodes that are still cost-effective.

aj: filing terraform PR and quota ticket now: https://go/repo/pulls/1234 (draft). tagging @maria @kai for review.

sabrina: quick question — do we need custom GPU driver build for L4? some kernels in canada-central images are older.

kai: driver compatibility check included in my terraform plan. will add kernel module detection script to the daemonset.

infra-bot: quota-request-created: ticket RG-5823, assigned to cloud-ops. ETA 72h.

maria: perfect. once quota is granted we can run canary with 10 pods for latency regression.

aj: thanks all — will update thread when quota approved and PR ready. :thumbsup:
